prompts.display_text: Pin the Laie Hawaii Temple, the first temple outside the continental US.
prompts.text_original: Drop a pin on the Laie Hawaii Temple, the first temple built outside the continental United States.
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org and ChurchofJesusChrist.org temple pages, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: President Joseph F. Smith dedicated the site on June 1, 1915, on the north shore of Oahu. President Heber J. Grant dedicated the temple on Thanksgiving Day, November 27, 1919. It was the first temple built outside the continental United States and the first in Polynesia.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country that was home to the first temple in its part of the world, outside the US.
prompts.text_original: A country that holds the first temple built in its continent or region outside the United States (Europe, Asia, Africa, South America, Central America, the Caribbean, the South Pacific, or outside the US at all).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology cross-checked with the Church's official temple list, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Temples spread beyond the United States one region at a time, starting with Canada in 1923. Each country here holds the first temple of a continent or region.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: São Paulo Brazil (dedicated 1978), the first temple in South America.

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: Cardston Alberta (dedicated 1923), the first temple outside the United States.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: Bern Switzerland (dedicated 1955), the first temple in Europe.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Tokyo Japan (dedicated 1980), the first temple in Asia.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: Hamilton New Zealand (dedicated 1958), the first temple in the South Pacific.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: Johannesburg South Africa (dedicated 1985), the first temple in Africa.

answers.name: Dominican Republic
answers.fact: Santo Domingo Dominican Republic (dedicated 2000), the first temple in the Caribbean.

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: Guatemala City Guatemala (dedicated 1984), the first temple in Central America.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose chronology names its first native mission president, called between 1975 and 2005.
prompts.text_original: A country whose chronology names the first citizen of that country to be called as a mission president (1975-2005).
prompts.citation: Global Histories (churchofjesuschrist.org), country chronologies and overviews, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Local leadership matured as native members took charge of missions: a Korean led the Pusan Mission in 1975, Jose Armando Sousa opened Peru Lima North in 1977, Costa Rican and Ecuadorian presidents followed in 1985, and Ukrainians, Belarusians and Ivorians led missions from 1996 to 2005.

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: 1975: the first Korean to serve as a mission president was called to preside over the newly organized Korean Pusan Mission.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: January 1, 1977: Jose Armando Sousa, the first Peruvian mission president, was assigned to the new Peru Lima North Mission.

answers.name: Ivory Coast
answers.fact: 2005: Norbert K. Ounleu began presiding over the Cote d'Ivoire Abidjan Mission, the first Ivorian mission president.

answers.name: Costa Rica
answers.fact: July 1985: Manuel Najera, the first Costa Rican called as a mission president, was assigned to Honduras.

answers.name: Ecuador
answers.fact: July 1985: Cesar Hugo Cacuango became the first Ecuadorian to serve as a mission president, in Maracaibo, Venezuela.

answers.name: Ukraine
answers.fact: 1996: Oleksandr Manzhos was called as president of the Ukraine Donetsk Mission, the first mission president from independent Ukraine.

answers.name: Belarus
answers.fact: July 2004: Mikhail Davydik was called as the first mission president from Belarus, to the Russia Samara Mission.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country that sent out its first full-time missionary from among its own members between 1952 and 1969.
prompts.text_original: A country whose first full-time missionary called from among its own members began service between 1952 and 1969.
prompts.citation: Global Histories (churchofjesuschrist.org), country chronologies and overviews, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.note: Each of these countries called its first missionary from its own members between 1952 and 1969.
prompts.summary: A country's own members serving missions marks a turning point. Costa Rica and Japan called their first in 1952, Fiji in 1955, South Korea in 1956, Taiwan in 1959, South Africa in 1966, Bolivia in 1968 and Thailand in 1969.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: In 1952 Hide Kishigami became the first missionary called from Japan to teach the Japanese people.

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: In 1956 Lee Young Bum became the first full-time missionary from South Korea.

answers.name: Bolivia
answers.fact: On August 14, 1968, Carlos Pedraja became the first full-time missionary called from Bolivia.

answers.name: Costa Rica
answers.fact: In 1952 Sister Arredondo and Sister Peralta became the first missionaries from Costa Rica.

answers.name: Thailand
answers.fact: In January 1969 a Thai convert became the first local full-time missionary in Thailand.

answers.name: Taiwan
answers.fact: In 1959 Chiu Siou-ping (Donna) became the first local missionary from Taiwan.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: On February 7, 1966, the first young missionaries from South Africa were called.

answers.name: Fiji
answers.fact: In 1955 a Fijian member left to serve a mission in Samoa, becoming the first full-time missionary from Fiji.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where the New Testament itself places one of the Twelve or Barnabas, Paul aside.
prompts.text_original: A present-day country where the New Testament itself places one of the Twelve or Barnabas, Paul aside
prompts.note: Site is in the West Bank or Gaza; a player may reasonably pin ISR as well.
prompts.summary: Set Paul aside and the Twelve still travel. Peter raised Tabitha at Joppa and went to Samaria with John, John wrote from Patmos, and Barnabas sailed home to Cyprus (Acts 15:39). The Gospels place the disciples beyond the Jordan with Jesus and in the coasts of Tyre and Sidon (Matthew 15:21).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Peter raised Tabitha at Joppa and stayed with Simon the tanner (Acts 9:36-43).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Peter and John were sent to the new believers in Samaria (Acts 8:14).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Peter was rebuked by Paul at Antioch, and Barnabas preached across Pisidia and Lycaonia (Galatians 2:11; Acts 13-14).

answers.name: Cyprus
answers.fact: Barnabas took Mark and sailed to his home island of Cyprus (Acts 15:39).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: John wrote Revelation on the isle of Patmos (Revelation 1:9).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: The disciples were with Jesus beyond Jordan when word came of Lazarus (John 10:40; 11:7-16).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: The disciples were with Jesus in the coasts of Tyre and Sidon when the Canaanite woman came (Matthew 15:21-23).
